about: Cincuenta comes from Eguren Ugarte, a family winery in Páganos, beneath the medieval hilltop town of Laguardia in Rioja Alavesa. The Eguren family has made wine here since 1870 and is now in its sixth generation, led by sisters Asun and Mercedes Eguren. Their father, Victorino Eguren Ugarte, who died in 2023, built the modern bodega, with some two kilometres of cellars dug into the hillside and a small hotel overlooking the vines and the Sierra de Cantabria.

This is pure Tempranillo, grown on the family’s clay-limestone slopes at a modest yield of about 6,000 kilos per hectare. The grapes are destemmed and crushed, then fermented for about fifteen days at 25–28°C with daily pump-overs. The wine spends fourteen months in a mix of American and French oak, racked three times along the way, and rests at least six months in bottle before release. It is bottled without fining or filtration.

The winery’s note for the bottling describes ripe raspberry, strawberry and subtle oak on the nose, and plum, cherry and raspberry on the palate, finishing fresh with well-structured tannins. James Suckling, who scored the 2017 at 92 points, noted plums, cherries, earth and sweet spice, with chalky tannins and bright acidity. It is a medium-bodied Rioja that he judged ready to drink or hold.
facts: 14 months in American and French oak, plus at least 6 months in bottle
